text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert: Verdant (enterprise, VPC) — us-west dedicated pool 'verdant-dp-uswest' showing sustained 5xx spikes and queue growth > 90%. Ticket #INC-2026-558. Automated mitigation triggers exhausted. Paging on-call.

ryan (oncall): saw it. I'm oncall, joining. Any customer visible impact?

maya (sre-lead): yes, telemetry shows ~30% of requests for Verdant hitting 500s, latency jump to >2.5s. Error signatures point to KV cache pressure on the us-west pool; warm capacity health is OK but not auto-draining.

jules (eng-runtime): stack traces show repeated OOM-ish eviction logs in the inference runtime, but not a kernel panic. Continuous batching queues are growing and backpressure is cascading. Might be model-serving hot spot for a popular model variant Verdant pinned to.

ryan (oncall): immediate plan options: 1) shift traffic to Verdant's warm pool in us-east, 2) DNS cutover to a compatible regional endpoint, 3) increase dedicated pool capacity (slow). Prefer quick shift + low-TTL DNS.

maya (sre-lead): agree. Execute regional traffic shift to us-east warm pool, canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% if green. We'll keep the us-west pool in read-only to avoid state churn. Need netops help for private DNS updates and VIP announcement.

zoe (acct-sd): pinging Verdant CSM and security contact. Will ask them to expect connection changes and to whitelist new IPs if they have egress filters. I'll draft an impact note to send after first canary.

ivan (netops): ready to assist. Do you want us to pre-announce a VIP in us-east or handle DNS TTL low cutover? If they use private route tables we may need to update VPC peering entries too.

jules (eng-runtime): steps I'll run now:

```
# Redwood CLI plan (internal)
rwctl tenant shift-traffic --tenant verdant --from us-west --to us-east --pool warm --mode gradual --step 10 --verify-curl "https://verdant.internal/api/v1/health" 
# Verify canary after each step
```

ryan (oncall): run the shift, jules. Set TTL to 30s on the customer-facing DNS before first step. maya, once 10% green for 5m, we bump to 50. If errors spike, rollback to 0 immediately and mark root cause.

jules (eng-runtime): kicking off step 1 -> shifting 10% now. Will post curl results.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy/verdant-routing v2026.03 initiated by jules — step=10% — started 1768854337

jules (eng-runtime): CURL check after canary:
```
curl -sS -D - https://verdant.internal/api/v1/health -H "Host: api.verdant.prod" | head -n 20
# HTTP/1.1 200 OK
# X-Request-Id: req-abc-123
# body: {"status":"ok","region":"us-east","lat_ms":120}
```

maya (sre-lead): 10% looks healthy, CPU and queue depth stable on us-east. Errors in us-west dropped ~12% overall. Proceed to 50%.

ryan (oncall): doing TTL change now. Support-run: set api.verdant.prod A records TTL=30. ivan, can you prepare VIP announcement if DNS doesn't propagate?

ivan (netops): prepping BGP/peering announcement for us-east VIP. If DNS fails to reach on-prem caches we'll announce and then coordinate with Verdant infra team for their eBGP.

zoe (acct-sd): message draft to customer: "We detected errors impacting your us-west inference pool. We're shifting traffic to a warm pool in us-east (incremental) to restore throughput. Minimal interruption expected; we'll notify after each step." OK to send after 50%?

maya (sre-lead): wait till 50% green then send. Also ask Verdant to temporarily relax egress ACLs for IPs in 3 ranges: 34.78.0.0/18, 34.79.0.0/18, 34.80.0.0/18 (us-east warm pool).

jules (eng-runtime): shifting to 50% now. Step took ~45s — new canary results: 200s for canary subset, latency stable. Logs show no new eviction patterns on us-east.

ryan (oncall): send customer note, zoe. Also update status page: "Verdant enterprise VPC — degraded in us-west, shifting traffic to us-east; mitigation in progress."

zoe (acct-sd): sent. Customer reply: "Thanks. We're allowing the new IP ranges; please advise when complete so we can flip internal routes."

maya (sre-lead): continue to 100% if next 5m stable. Meanwhile open a ticket to pin model variant or reduce batch size for us-west to avoid repeat.

jules (eng-runtime): 100% shift in progress. Post-shift smoke curl:
```
curl -sS https://verdant.internal/api/v1/predict -H "Host: api.verdant.prod" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' | jq '.model_response'
# returns inference result; latency 130ms
```
deploy-bot: route-shift/verdant v2026.03 completed -> to=us-east percentage=100 completed_at=1768854390

ryan (oncall): us-west pool marked for investigation but traffic drained. Watch for regression alarms and keep rollback plan ready.

ivan (netops): VIP announcement deferred; DNS propagation completed globally within ~2m due to low TTL — no BGP change needed.

zoe (acct-sd): Verdant confirmed service is back for their end-to-end tests. They asked for a post-incident call at +1h.

maya (sre-lead): assign follow-ups: 1) eng-runtime to investigate eviction root cause (jules), 2) SRE to create RCA draft (maya), 3) AE to log customer notes (zoe). I'll schedule postmortem.

ryan (oncall): handing off to maya for long-running RCA. I'll stay on standby for 30m in case rollback needed. Closing incident channel when RCA thread opened. (reacts: :white_check_mark:)

jules (eng-runtime): quick note: found a problematic model variant config that increased KV cache pressure with some request patterns. WIP patch to limit per-request KV retention and reduce batch size. Will attach reproducer logs to RCA.

incident-bot: incident INC-2026-558 status -> mitigated (traffic shifted), severity -> P1 -> monitoring.

maya (sre-lead): thanks team. Zoe please confirm customer follow-up time and collect any logs they can share. We'll include timeline and mitigations in the postmortem.

zoe (acct-sd): confirmed call with Verdant at 18:30 PT. I'll add attendees.

ryan (oncall): logging handoff: maya owns RCA, jules owns fix & deploy, ivan keeps netops watch for any peering anomalies. Closing active paging.

(End of thread)
